answer: An extracted dependency edge is traceable only when the edge record carries its own evidence, not when the edge merely appears in a graph, a search snippet or a visualization. Read together, the corpus requires six elements. (1) Source identity and version: the source file/version or admitted document, and an immutable or revision-bound knowledge snapshot plus document ID; for lineage edges, versioned source dataset namespace/name/version. (2) Extraction provenance: the inference/extraction method and its date, or the transformation job/version/run that produced the relation, with the relation meaning retained. (3) A bounded, canonical locator: a bounded section or range with a canonical local or public source reference, rather than a snippet or a "related document" navigation hint. (4) Separate status states: evidence confidence and verification freshness recorded as distinct states, whether the linked source was actually inspected, and unknown field-level mappings marked unknown instead of inferred. (5) A temporal and update contract: snapshot membership, edge freshness, a deprecation/removal rule and an owner for conflict resolution; stale edges are marked stale or unknown rather than silently deleted or re-asserted, and the historical reason a relationship once existed is kept. (6) Preserved contradiction: document identity, supported claim, citation/source version, date or revision, applicability and unresolved contradictions; a mixed-snapshot conclusion is rejected or its unresolved evidence disclosed. Limits: such a record establishes attribution, not truth — revision drift can invalidate a valid-looking path, a pinned result alone cannot certify semantic truth, and the authoritative source is still needed for consequential claims.
